t: The first sentence of subsection (a) of section 1309 of the National Flood Insurance Act of 1968 (42 U.S.C. 4016(a)), as amended by the National Flood Insurance Program Further Enhanced Borrowing Authority Act of 2005 (Public Law 109–106; 119 Stat. 2288), is amended by striking “$18,500,000,000” and inserting “$20,775,000,000”.

fable.w: This section only raises the dollar ceiling on borrowing authority under the National Flood Insurance Act. There is no tempting reading here: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: is amended by striking “$18,500,000,000” and inserting “$20,775,000,000”

opus.w: This section only raises the borrowing limit in the National Flood Insurance Act from $18.5 billion to $20.775 billion. It gives no one outside the federal government any role in a federal decision: there is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation or right to sue. The fact that it amends a public program does not, by itself, create any participation.
opus.s: is amended by striking “$18,500,000,000” and inserting “$20,775,000,000”.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a simple appropriation amendment that changes a dollar figure. It does not establish any process for consulting with, coordinating with, or receiving input from parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory committees, public hearings, comment periods, or consultation requirements mentioned.
qwen_chat.s: The first sentence of subsection (a) of section 1309 of the National Flood Insurance Act of 1968 (42 U.S.C. 4016(a)), as amended by the National Flood Insurance Program Further Enhanced Borrowing Authority Act of 2005 (Public Law 109–106; 119 Stat. 2288), is amended by striking “$18,500,000,000” and inserting “$20,775,000,000”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing a funding limit could indirectly affect public participation if it changes the scope of a program, but the text itself contains no procedural requirement for consultation, comment, or involvement of outside parties. It is purely a numerical amendment to an appropriation limit.
